**PotentialNoise 2.3.0**

- **SIGNAL**: four things to play, one tap each. **PINK NOISE** (as before), **TEST TONE** (a steady sine at 1 kHz, 100, 60 or 40 Hz, at the LEVEL you pick: 1 kHz for gain staging, the low ones to hear how far down your speakers go), **OCTAVE BAND** (pink noise in one octave only, 31 Hz to 16 kHz, to balance the tracks in that range) and **SPEAKER CHECK** (left, right, both in phase, both out of phase, 2 seconds each, with the tip line saying which: a quick check that your speakers are the right way round and wired in phase).
- Switching signal, tone, band, channels or range while it plays fades out and back in, so there are no clicks.
- The GUIDE page switches to pink noise when it starts.
- The settings under SIGNAL change with it. Three parameters were added at the end of the list (Signal, Tone, Octave Band); saved projects open as before.

**Downloads**
- **`PotentialNoise-2.3.0-akai-vst2.zip`**: for **MPC OS 3.10.1 or later**, any standalone MPC (32-bit and 64-bit). Turn on **External Plugin Support** in Preferences → Enhancements (Beta), unzip, and copy the folder into **VST2 Plugins** at the top of a drive. See the [install guide](https://github.com/PotentialBreakfast/mpc-vst-potentialnoise/blob/main/INSTALL-GUIDE.md).
- **`PotentialNoise-2.3.0-mpc-sdk.zip`**: the same plugin folder in the Open MPC catalog's 3.10.1 format (one folder for every MPC).
- **`PotentialNoise-2.3.0-mpc-armv7.zip`**: for Gen1 MPCs with the community plugin set-up on older MPC OS 3.x. Install it with the [Open MPC](https://open-mpc.github.io/) installer app, or follow `INSTALL.md` inside the zip. Save your project first, because installing restarts the MPC.
- **`PotentialNoise-2.3.0-mpc-aarch64.zip`**: the same for Gen2 MPCs (MPC Live III, XL), installed by the Open MPC Plugin Manager.

Install it one way only. Ideas, bugs and criticism are all welcome: [open an issue](https://github.com/PotentialBreakfast/mpc-vst-potentialnoise/issues/new/choose).
